newsitem.title: CHINA: China key coal mines see 110 mln yuan profit in H1.
newsitem.headline: China key coal mines see 110 mln yuan profit in H1.

text.p: China's key coal mine enterprises reported a profit of 110 million yuan ($13 million) in the first half of this year, pulling the long-ailing industry out of the red, the People's Daily said on Tuesday.
Business turnover of major state-owned mines had jumped 15.5 percent to 22.1 billion yuan in the first six months, the newspaper said.
Actual profits of such mines were 110 million yuan in the period, pulling the sector into the black after it incurred losses over the last several years, the newspaper said.
China's key coal mines had lost nearly 6.0 billion yuan in 1992, the newspaper said but did gave no figures for intervening years.
The sector's positive first half performance meant it had met a target set by the State Council, or cabinet, to start turning profits a year and a half early, it said.
This year, 58 of 93 key state coal mines had begun to turn profits by reducing coal output and boosting product quality, it said.
State coal enterprises also cut payrolls by 188,000 employees in the first half of this year to try to raise efficiency, it said but gave no further details.
In the first half of this year, output of key state-owned coal mines dropped by 2.54 million tonnes or 0.99 percent compared with the same period last year, it said.
China produced 675.8 million tonnes of coal in the first half of this year, up 1.9 percent from the same year-ago period, latest official figures show.
